original_question: Divide 10 into two numbers so that, after dividing each number by the other, adding the two quotients, squaring that sum, and multiplying by one of the two numbers, the result is a prescribed given number.
target_in_paper: The draft is targeting Section 5.4, Problem 5 of the paper's list of Ibn al-Khawwām's thirty-three problems: the problem about decomposing 10 into two numbers, forming the two mutual quotients, adding them, squaring the sum, and multiplying by one chosen part to obtain a prescribed value. Section 5.4 explicitly places it among the "Equations of degree Four or Higher." ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/html/2511.08400v1))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the core official statement very closely: the total 10, the two reciprocal quotients, the addition of those quotients, the squaring step, the final multiplication by one part, and the fact that the output is a prescribed target value. In substance, it is very near the paper's Problem 5. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/html/2511.08400v1))
missing_details: The paper's overall arithmetic framing is about solving such problems in integers or rationals, but your draft does not specify the ambient domain of the unknowns; for a stand-alone paper-faithful formulation, one should say explicitly that the question asks for rational solutions. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/html/2511.08400v1))
The phrase "divide 10 into two numbers" should be formalized as introducing variables x and y with x+y=10. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/html/2511.08400v1))

Because each number is divided by the other, one must impose the hidden denominator condition xy≠0 (equivalently x≠0 and y≠0). This is implicit in the wording but absent from the draft. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/html/2511.08400v1))

The phrase "multiply by one of the two numbers" is ambiguous unless a distinguished variable is fixed in advance; a precise version should say, for example, that x is the part used in the final multiplication. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/html/2511.08400v1))

The prescribed output should be introduced as an explicit parameter, e.g. a given rational number N, together with the quantifier "given N, determine/classify all solutions." Your draft gestures at this but does not formalize it. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/html/2511.08400v1))

Section 5.4 classifies this as a quartic-or-higher equation problem, so the sharpened question should remain this exact solvability problem and not be broadened into a different algebraic or Diophantine variant. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/html/2511.08400v1))

No homogeneity condition, nilpotency hypothesis, degree-4 homogeneous-polynomial setup, or "for all sufficiently large m" quantifier belongs to this target statement; those notions are simply inapplicable here and should not be imported. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/html/2511.08400v1))

The paper's displayed wording does not explicitly add a positivity restriction on the two parts; if positivity is intended, it would need to be stated separately, but omitting it is closer to the paper as written. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/html/2511.08400v1))
refined_question: Given a prescribed rational number N, determine all rational solutions (x,y) with x+y=10 and xy≠0 such that x((x/y)+(y/x))^2=N, where x is the part chosen for the final multiplication. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/html/2511.08400v1))
justification: This rewrite stays as close as possible to the paper's actual Problem 5 in Section 5.4 while adding only the hidden data needed to make the question mathematically stand-alone: named variables, the equation x+y=10, the nonzero-denominator condition, a fixed choice of which part is used in the last multiplication, and the paper-wide rational-solution framing. I have not broadened the scope beyond the exact problem stated in the paper. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/html/2511.08400v1))
